A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Model Tensor Planning and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A.1–A.5. Their corresponding material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original robotic simulation experiments, parameter ablations, and implementation timing measurements in Section 4 and Appendix A.5.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds runtime measurements across tasks and batch sizes in Tables 6–8.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 retain the same tensor sampling, spline interpolation, beta-mixing, and softmax-weighted elite updates. Added sampling explanations and tuning recommendations do not introduce a new procedure. The corrected preliminary CEM equation does not establish a change to the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Navigation, Crane, Cube-In-Hand, G1-Walk, G1-Standup, PushT, and Walker with unchanged task definitions and randomization coverage. The new runtime tables reuse existing tasks without adding a distinct task or environmental scenario.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the retained experiments: CEM in Figure 1, and MPPI, PS, Diffusion Evolution, and OpenAI-ES in the main comparisons and Table 5. The added timing tables measure already evaluated MPPI and OpenAI-ES; no existing comparison loses a comparator.

E3.justification: Tables 6–8 add a runtime protocol using batch sizes 64, 128, and 256 on four existing tasks with an RTX 4090. The original RTX 3090, batch-128 G1-Standup benchmark remains. Existing task costs, simulation settings, and hyperparameter tables are unchanged; the new timings are not same-setting improvements over Table 5.

E4.justification: The new timing tables examine how compilation and planning costs depend on rollout batch size across tasks, adding a limited computational scaling analysis. Existing elite-count, mixing-rate, spline-degree, graph-size, and softmax ablation results remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Appendix A.5 changes the reported seed count for the B-spline degree ablation from five to four, although Figure 7 is unchanged; this does not establish that experiments were rerun. New Tables 6–8 report five-seed averages with planning-time uncertainty, but show JIT times only as means.

E6.justification: The original nine figures and Tables 1–5 retain their results. Tables 6–8 add compilation and planning times for MTP-Akima, MPPI, and OpenAI-ES. For example, MTP-Akima's Cube-In-Hand planning time is 8.1 ± 0.3 ms at batch 64 and 14.7 ± 0.8 ms at batch 256. These extend runtime evidence without revising task-performance findings.

T1.justification: Equation 4 corrects the elite-sample mean and variance denominators from B and B−1 to E and E−1. The path-coverage theorem, its proof, and Appendix A.2's entropy arguments remain unchanged. Graph-symbol changes are only notational.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and principal conclusions retain the same claims about tensor sampling, asymptotic coverage and entropy, beta-mixing, and vectorized real-time control. Additional runtime evidence and deployment discussion do not redefine the central contributions.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations of diminishing returns from increasing N, task-dependent exploration needs, and runtime scaling. It clarifies the timing benchmark's limited scope and adds actuator, state-estimation, and communication constraints for deployment. The explicit statement that MTP does not support model uncertainty is removed, while the fixed-dynamics limitation remains.

D1.justification: V2 adds graph-size and mixing-rate guidance, specifies RTX 4090 hardware for the new timings, and clarifies that the retained timing benchmark measures one sampling/rollout/update cycle. Figure 1 removes the direct repository link and open-source implementation statement while retaining the video-site link; actual repository availability cannot be inferred.

R1.justification: V2 adds explicit attribution to Watson and Peters (2023) in the spline motivation and MPPI discussion, and links spline dimensionality reduction to Carvalho et al. This modestly refines connections to prior work. The bibliography retains the same works; the Carvalho and GTMP publication updates are not new references.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized wording and notation clarifications, corrects an author affiliation, expands practical explanations, and renames Appendix A.4 to include discussions. It adds a Broader Impact Statement, separates the limitations heading, and removes acknowledgments. Most prose and the overall section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds three runtime tables, widens Figure 1, clarifies Figure 4's caption, and relocates Algorithm 1 and appendix displays through reflow. The original figure contents are retained, without a substantial redesign of the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: V2 modestly improves mathematical accuracy through Equation 4 and strengthens practical evaluation through Tables 6–8. Clarifying the timing benchmark's scope and deployment requirements also makes the real-time claims easier to assess. These benefits are limited by unchanged core theoretical and task-performance evidence, and removal of the direct code link reduces reproducibility information. Overall, the gains support a limited improvement.
